`minimal prompt → single careful diff pass → ≤15 findings`

You are reviewing a pull request for real bugs. Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

Review the diff as a careful senior engineer would: read every hunk, open the surrounding files for context as needed (Read, Grep, git log/blame/show), and hunt for correctness issues — wrong or inverted conditions, off-by-one, null/undefined dereference, missing `await`, dropped error handling, removed guards or validations, broken callers of changed functions, races. Prefer real failure modes over style; every finding needs a concrete scenario in which the code misbehaves.

When you are done, submit at most 15 findings via the ReportFindings tool, filling its fields as defined — for each: the file path and start line, a severity, and a comment that states the issue and the concrete scenario in which the code misbehaves. Quality over quantity: include everything you genuinely believe is a real issue, and nothing you don't.

After the tool call, also restate the findings in your final reply — one line each, `file:line — summary` — so they stay visible in sessions that do not render tool output.

1	# STORY-006: Close the holes in the customization seam
2	
3	## User Story
4	
5	As a downstream consumer of this template repo (e.g. test-framework-template, android-wifi-mcp),
6	I want every project-specific value to actually resolve from `project-profile.md` — and to be
7	   told when one doesn't,
8	So that I never have to edit a shipped unit to get the behaviour I declared, and upstream
9	   improvements still reach me without a merge conflict over my own customizations.
10	
11	## The Need
12	
13	STORY-005 shipped the customization seam and it works. Nine `dw-*` commands are byte-identical
14	across two downstreams that have never coordinated; the runner absorbs all of its differences in
15	its profile without touching a single command. The rule — *edit the profile, not the units* — is
16	sound and is holding.
17	
18	But the seam has holes. A few values never made it out of the command text, and where a unit
19	names its own value, the profile is inert: a project can set the value, nothing follows, and the
20	only way to get the behaviour it declared is to edit the shipped file. That edit then looks like
21	the downstream drifting when it is really working around us.
22	
23	Two downstreams have now paid for this, independently:
24	
25	| Value | Where it's still named inside a unit | Who tripped over it | What they had to do |
26	|---|---|---|---|
27	| images dir | `doc-gen-readme.md`, `rules/doc-workflow.md` | test-framework-template | rewrote the command to point at its own diagrams dir |
28	| drift anchor (`story_hash`) | `qw-cases.md`, `qw-review-cases.md` | android-wifi-mcp | replaced hash drift with a derived chain check, then edited both commands |
29	
30	One of those values is also simply **wrong**. The profile declares an images dir this repo does
31	not have; the six diagrams it actually ships live somewhere else entirely, and the README links
32	them from there. So `doc-gen-readme` run here today writes into a directory the repo doesn't use.
33	That breaks the profile's own promise — that its defaults "reproduce this repo's current
34	behaviour" — and it is the promise the whole seam rests on, because it is what makes adoption a
35	no-op until a project opts in.
36	
37	Underneath both is the same gap: **nothing checks that a unit doesn't name a value the profile
38	owns.** STORY-005 swept 18 units by hand and got most of them; there is no pass that would catch
39	the ones it missed, or the next one someone writes. So a leak stays invisible until a downstream
40	trips over it — which is the expensive place to find it, because by then the workaround is
41	already committed in someone else's repo and reads as their mistake.
42	
43	## Success Looks Like
44	
45	- A downstream changes the images dir or the drift anchor in its profile, and the commands
46	  follow — with no unit edited.
47	- No shipped command, skill, or rule names a value the profile owns.
48	- Every default the profile declares matches what this repo actually does, and that agreement is
49	  something anyone can check rather than take on trust.
50	- The workarounds in `test-framework-template` and `android-wifi-mcp` become unnecessary: those
51	  files can match upstream again without either project losing the behaviour it chose.
52	- A new leak is caught when it is introduced, not when a downstream trips over it months later.
53	- We know the known leaks are the whole list — not just the ones a downstream happened to hit.
54	
55	## Open Questions
56	
57	- How is "no unit names a profile-owned value" actually checked — a question added to
58	  `reviewing-artifacts`, a line in the rules, or something runnable in CI? (decided in `dw-plan`)
59	- The drift anchor is a *mechanism*, not just a field name — android-wifi-mcp swapped hashing for
60	  a derived link check. Does the profile declare the mechanism, or only the front-matter fields,
61	  with the mechanism left to the project's own layer?
62	- Do the three known leaks represent the whole problem, or does a re-audit of all 18 units from
63	  STORY-005 turn up more?
64	- For the images dir: does the corrected default become this repo's real diagrams layout, or does
65	  the declared default stay as-is with this repo setting its own value like any other project?
66	- Is the profile's "defaults reproduce this repo's behaviour" promise worth enforcing generally,
67	  or is the images dir a one-off to fix and move on?
68

73	- Issues: none

1	# `docs/stories/` — the story format
2	
3	Each story is a **readable markdown document** that lives here. It states a **need** — a
4	goal, not a spec — in the user's terms. The markdown is the *canonical* record of *why* a
5	piece of work exists; it is the stable anchor the plan and task issues trace back to.
6	`dw-story` writes these; `dw-review-story` reviews them.
7	
8	The **how** — the agreed approach and the work itself — lives in the **plan issue** and the
9	**task issues** on GitHub, **not here**. A story says what's needed and what success looks
10	like; it does not freeze a design. Keeping the *how* out of the story is what lets the
11	approach evolve on the issues without rewriting the need.
12	
13	## One file = one story
14	
15	```
16	docs/stories/
17	  STORY-001.md   # one story: the need + success, nothing about the build
18	  STORY-002.md
19	```
20	
21	- File + id follow the project's `STORY-XXX` convention — `STORY-NNN.md`, no slug (see `.claude/rules/project-profile.md`).
22	- A story is **plain markdown — no front-matter.** It opens with `# STORY-NNN: <Title>`.
23	
24	## Sections
25	
26	In order, every story carries:
27	
28	```markdown
29	# STORY-NNN: <specific title>
30	
31	## User Story
32	As <role>, I want <goal>, so that <benefit>.
33	
34	## The Need
35	<the problem behind the request, in the user's terms — the why, not the how>
36	
37	## Success Looks Like
38	- <an outcome someone could observe once this is delivered>
39	
40	## Open Questions
41	- <what's genuinely unresolved — or "none known"; deferred to the plan/issues>
42	
43	## Status
44	- Created: <date>
45	```
46	
47	- **User Story** — a real role, action, and a benefit that isn't just the action restated.
48	- **The Need** — the problem and why it matters, in the reader's terms. No files, APIs, or
49	  step-by-step build detail.
50	- **Success Looks Like** — observable, user-facing outcomes — not implementation steps.
51	- **Open Questions** — the uncertain *how*, deferred to the plan/issues. Empty-because-skipped
52	  is a finding, not a pass.
53	- **Status** — the record below.
54	
55	## Status conventions
56	
57	The Status block grows as the work moves, linking the story to its GitHub artifacts:
58	
59	```markdown
60	## Status
61	
62	- **Completed: <date>** — <one line on what shipped> (PRs #<n>, #<n>).
63	- Created: <date>
64	- Plan: #<plan-issue>
65	- Issues: ✅ #<n> (PR #<n>), ✅ #<n>, …
66	```
67	
68	- `Created:` on every story; the **bold `Completed:`** line is added (first) once delivered.
69	- `Plan:` is the `[STORY-XXX] Plan` issue (`dw-plan`); `Issues:` are the tasks (`dw-tasks`),
70	  ✅ when closed.
71	
72	## Goal, not spec
73	
74	`dw-review-story` gates exactly this: the story is **complete** (every section present and
75	substantive) and stays a **goal document** — no leaked implementation, success written as
76	outcomes, the technical *how* left to the issues. A story decidable by someone who won't
77	build it has passed.
78	
79	## Traceability
80	
81	- **story → plan/tasks:** the `Status` block's `Plan:` and `Issues:` lines.
82	- **plan/task → story:** the issue's `[STORY-XXX]` title prefix and `Part of` link.
83	
84	No hand-maintained index — the links live in the files and the issues, and resolve by
85	path / `gh`.
86	
87	## Beyond the story (the plan + issues)
88	
89	The approach, the task breakdown, and the build history are the **plan issue** and **task
90	issues'** concern, not this format's. The story records the need; the issues carry the how
91	(see `.claude/rules/dev-workflow.md`).
92

5	---
6	
7	# project-profile
8	
9	The one place a downstream project declares its specifics. The shipped commands and
10	skills state their *intent* and resolve any project-specific value — a path, an ID
11	scheme, a label, an integration, a format, an audience — **from this file**, instead of
12	hardcoding it. Customize a workflow by editing this file, not the units.
13	
14	**How a unit uses it.** Where a command or skill would otherwise bake in a value, it
15	points at the matching section here (e.g. "create the *plan* label — see
16	project-profile → Labels"). The values below are the **defaults**: they reproduce this
17	repo's current behaviour, so a project that changes nothing behaves exactly as it does
18	now. Adoption is opt-in — change a line here and every unit follows.
19	
20	**What belongs here vs. not.** This file is for **declarative** customization — a value
21	or a list. A whole **procedure** (e.g. how to publish to Confluence and review the
22	render) is *not* a value; it belongs in its own project-owned skill, never crammed into
23	a general unit. Lists → here; procedures → a project skill. This is the rules files'
24	"what this owns vs. what it hands off" boundary, made concrete.
25	
26	---
27	
28	## Paths
29	
30	- stories dir: `docs/stories/`
31	- tests dir: `docs/tests/`
32	- images dir: `docs/images/`
33	- story format contract: `docs/stories/README.md`
34	- test format contract: `docs/tests/README.md`
35	
36	## ID schemes
37	
38	- story id: `STORY-XXX` (zero-padded sequential, e.g. `STORY-001`)
39	- scenario id: `TS-NN`
40	- case id: `TC-NN`
41	- title prefixes: `[STORY-XXX] Plan` · `[STORY-XXX] Test Plan` · `[STORY-XXX] <task>`
42	
43	## Labels
44	
45	Names the workflow uses; colours where the workflow pins one (`#hex`), otherwise the
46	project's choice.
47	
48	- plan: `plan` (`#5319e7`)
49	- test plan: `test-plan` (`#006b75`)
50	- priority: `priority:high` · `priority:medium` · `priority:low`
51	- type: `feature` · `enhancement` · `bug` · `docs`
52	- status: `status:in-progress` · `status:needs-review` · `status:blocked`
53	
54	## Linking & branch
55	
56	- story back-reference (in titles/bodies): `[STORY-XXX]`
57	- plan back-reference (task → plan): `Part of #<plan>`
58	- issue closure (PR → issue): `Fixes #N` / `Closes #N`
59	- feature branch name: `issue-<N>-<slug>`
60	
61	## Git
62	
63	- default branch: *derive it* (`gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef -q .defaultBranchRef.name`), don't assume `main`
64	- merge strategy: `--merge` (preserve history; switch to `--squash` only if the project requires)
65	
66	## Front-matter & format contract (test docs)
67	
68	- test-doc filename: `TS-NN-<slug>.md` in the tests dir
69	- front-matter fields: `id, title, namespace, story, story_hash, plan, issue, status`
70	- story hash: `sha256` of the story file (`sha256sum`)
71	- default status: `green`
72	
73	## Docs & diagrams
74	
75	- README output: `README.md`
76	- diagram policy: SVG source committed + rendered to PNG (no Mermaid / inline diagram blocks)
77	- images dir: `docs/images/` (also under Paths)
78	
79	## Review semantics
80	
81	- canonical format (source of truth): `markdown`
82	- live integrations: `GitHub` — tools the project genuinely uses; coupling to one
83	  listed here is correct, not drift. (A downstream adds its own, e.g. Jira, Confluence,
84	  TestLink.)
85	- deliverable (triggers a paired review): a unit that *produces or changes* an output —
86	  by name (`create-`/`sync-`/`publish-`/`draft-`/`init-`) or as a producing gerund skill
87	  (`planning-…`, `drafting-…`)
88	- audience (human-read docs): engineers and newcomers
